analysis.title: US Fed: mission not yet accomplished. Two more hikes to come (Chart of the Week)
key_insights: Berenberg changes its Fed call. Instead of a final 25bp hike on 9 December, it now expects a further 25bp move on 17 March 2027, taking the Fed funds target range to 4.25-4.5%.
Core consumer prices rose 0.3% mom in October, which Berenberg reads as underlying domestic inflationary pressure beyond the pass-through of higher oil prices.
The US economy has regained momentum this year after a lull in late 2025. Payrolls are on track to rise by about 1m this year versus 0.1m last year.

The unemployment rate fell from 4.4% in late 2025 to 4.1%, and average weekly hours rose from 34.1 at the beginning of 2025 to 34.4. Berenberg reads this as labour demand outstripping labour supply, with immigration clampdown limiting supply.
Average hourly earnings growth slowed to 3.1% yoy in October from 3.9% a year earlier. Berenberg says wages often react with a lag, so the Fed has to take the risk of more wage inflation seriously.

Almost two-thirds of the 2.1% yoy rise in Q3 real GDP comes from a 30% yoy surge in information processing equipment investment and a 13% rise in software investment. Including data centres and energy supply, and net of IT equipment imports, more than one-third of US demand growth is tied to AI investment.

Private consumption rose 2.5% yoy and remains the major driver of demand at face value. The personal savings rate fell to 4.1% in Q3 2026 from 5.2% a year earlier, suggesting consumers are spending wealth that depends on equity markets with heavy AI exposure.

Berenberg expects AI investment to moderate over 2027, as markets question returns and the midterm election results show resistance to data centre rollout. Lower oil prices in 2027 will not offset the lack of new household tax cuts, and higher Fed rates should help slow US growth to 1.5% in 2028.
Berenberg now projects the dollar at 1.20 per euro by end-2027 instead of 1.24, because of the revised Fed call, despite a worsening US fiscal position.

Tail risk: a burst in AI valuations could hit equities and AI-related bonds, cut AI investment, and force consumers to spend less. In an extreme case the Fed would have to cut rates significantly. Berenberg calls this unlikely but not impossible.
Berenberg expects the Fed to proceed cautiously: no 50bp move on 9 December and no more than one additional hike in 2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Points to underlying domestic inflationary pressure beyond oil pass-through, which supports further Fed hikes.
Down from 4.4% in late 2025, showing labour demand outstripping supply.
Down from 3.9% a year ago. No wage pressure yet, but wages lag the labour market.
Almost two-thirds of growth comes from information processing equipment and software investment.
Remains the major driver of demand at face value.
Down from 5.2% a year earlier, suggesting consumers are spending increased wealth tied to equity markets.
Compares with 0.1m added last year, showing a stronger labour market.
Berenberg's new forecast replaces the previous final 25bp hike on 9 December.
Previously 1.24. The higher Fed path limits dollar weakness.
Slowdown reflects moderating AI investment, no new tax cuts and higher Fed rates.

risk_factors: AI valuation bubble bursting, causing an equity and AI-related bond plunge and a sharp slowdown or drop in AI investment.
Evaporating wealth gains forcing US consumers to cut spending.
Wage inflation picking up with a lag if unemployment keeps falling.
Rising political resistance to data centre rollout, as shown in the midterm election results.

tension_points.bull_case: AI-related investment accounts for more than one-third of US demand growth, and the economy has regained momentum with payrolls on track for about 1m this year.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets question whether AI investment will generate returns that justify pricing. A bubble burst could hit equities and AI-related bonds, cut AI investment and force consumers to spend less, which could require significant Fed cuts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A burst in AI valuations causing a plunge in equities and AI-related bonds.
